title: Regional fallthrough slate and graceful unwind experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for a set of small experiments to exercise our regional fallthrough and graceful-unwind behaviors. The aim is to validate that when a regional capacity shortfall or increased latency occurs, our traffic steering and partial-degrade strategies keep latency SLOs for paying customers while minimizing error surface and cost.

Scope / Constraints:
- Target services: hosted generation API (text-completion route) and streaming chat route.
- Regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1 (simulate congestion in a single region).
- Duration: micro-experiments (48h window per hypothesis) with automated rollback.
- Do not exceed 20% global traffic change for any single experiment; customer-facing risks must be mitigated by quick fail gates.

Goals / Success metrics:
- No customer-facing error rate increase > 0.1% above baseline during experiment windows.
- Median p95 latency increase <= 10% for reserved-capacity customers; p99 targeted to remain within 20%.
- Fallthrough routing executes within 60s of region alarm (route flip observed in logs).
- Graceful-unwind (partial-degrade) reduces token spend by at least 12% when triggered without exceeding quality regression thresholds on smoke prompts.

Hypotheses to test:
1) Progressive fallthrough (10% -> 30% -> 60%) stabilizes latency faster than an immediate 60% shift because of KV-cache rewarm impacts.
2) Small partial-degrades (response truncation + soft-sampling) reduce cost with negligible quality drift on ephemeral workloads.
3) Telemetry sampling at the route level with adaptive backpressure gives earlier detection versus node-level CPU signals.

Experiment plan (high level):
- Preflight (T-72h): verification of smoke prompts, create canary teams, confirm observability dashboards and alert rules are active.
- T-24h: announce to SRE and CS on-call, scheduled postmortem owner assigned, run synthetic traffic baseline.
- T0: enable progressive fallthrough policy in staging for 1h; verify routing logs.
- T+2h: lift to production at min-volume (1% traffic) and exercise 3-step progression over next 6 hours for a small customer cohort.
- T+24h: full small-batch expansion (up to 15% traffic) conditioned on telemetry.
- T+48h: wind down and capture outputs, run postmortem template.

Preflight checklist:
- [ ] PR merging: runtime change PR#412 merged and smoke-tested on bench cluster (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Alerting: new composite alert 'regional-fallthrough-delta' created and tested (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Canary tokens: generated and hashed for prompt set A/B (owner: Daniel).
- [ ] Customer notice: CS-run advisory drafted for seats likely to see degraded throughput (owner: Elena).
- [ ] Runbook snippet: quick-rollback script and run commands in /ops/scripts/rollback-fallback.sh verified and staged.
- [ ] Data retention flags: telemetry retention for experiment increased to 14 days for easier analysis.

Rollout cadence (hourly plan for first 8 hours):
- Hour 0 (prod 1%): policy enabled, routing verifications and logs sanity check.
- Hour 1 (prod 3%): monitor p95/p99, error rate, cache hit ratio.
- Hour 2 (prod 7%): enable adaptive sampling for telemetry, run quality eval on smoke set.
- Hour 4 (prod 15%): if all green, continue. If error spike >0.05% or p99 > target, pause and rollback 30 mins.
- Hour 6 (prod 30%): expand only if red/amber metrics clear for 60m.
- Hour 8 (prod 60% for cohort): only by explicit on-call approval (SRE + Release Eng).

Short runbooks / operator cues:
- Immediate rollback triggers (auto):
  - sustained error rate > 0.1% for 5m
  - p99 latency doubled vs baseline for 3 consecutive 5m windows
  - circuit-breaker on model memory exceed -> auto-fallback to smaller variant
- Manual escalation: if customers report degradation via CS within 10m, preflight comms channel is #release-ops and page SRE.
- Fallback steps:
  1) Pause progressive progression and revert to previous routing weights
  2) If problem persists, enable traffic draining for region (graceful-unwind) and fallback to AU/US neighbors
  3) Execute rollback script and notify stakeholders

Observability checklist (queries & dashboards):
- Dashboard panels to verify: route-weight distribution, per-region latency histogram, KV-cache hit ratio, model-variant error map, token spend by customer tier.
- Suggested queries (to add to Runbook):
  - sum(rate(requests[1m])) by (region,route)
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le,region) (rate(latency_bucket[5m])))
  - increase(errors_total[10m]) / increase(requests_total[10m])
- Sampling: enable full tracing for 0.5% of fallthroughed requests, 100% trace for any error > 500 status.

Quality gating (smoke evals):
- Prompt set: 40 curated prompts covering long-context, few-shot, and streaming interactions.
- Thresholds: BLEU-like or embedding similarity check >= 0.92 on smoke set; human review if score drops 0.02 from baseline.

Communication templates (short):
- Internal alert: 'Experiment regional-fallthrough: rolling to 3% prod traffic. Watch p99 and error-rate. Triage in #release-ops.'
- Customer note (CS): 'We are running short maintenance experiments in region X that may alter routing for a subset of requests. Expected service continuity; reach out if you see persistent errors.'

Data collection & post-run analysis checklist:
- [ ] Export per-request trace ids for failed traces and store in experiment folder.
- [ ] Snapshot model-variant distribution and token spend (by customer tier) each 6h.
- [ ] Run quality regressions at T+24 and T+72 hours.
- [ ] Retrospective: runbook gaps and operator friction logged. Owner: Daniel.

Open questions / risks:
- How quickly will warmed KV caches move across regions during progressive shift? Need synthetic rewarm test (task RF-1134).
- Cost impact on burst routing vs long-term shift: projected delta unknown for >30% sustained shift. Finance to provide quick cost delta model.
- Customer-facing latency sensitivity differs by tier; need mapping from customers -> latency SLA to prioritize failover ordering.

Appendix: small hourly-calendar sample (48h)
Day 0:
  00:00 - preflight checks complete, enable in staging
  12:00 - 1% production for 60m (observe)
  13:00 - escalate to 3% if green
  15:00 - enable telemetry adaptive sampling
  18:00 - expand to 7% (cohort A)
Day 1:
  00:00 - expand to 15% (cohort B) if green; run full regression suite at 02:00
  12:00 - evaluate cost delta and qualitative notes; decision: continue/abort
  20:00 - begin graceful unwind tests (simulate neighbor draining)
Day 2:
  08:00 - wind down, snapshot datasets and run retrospective

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Marco: finalize bench harness to simulate KV-cache warm (RF-1134).
- Priya: add composite alert and test by firing synthetic anomaly.
- Elena: coordinate CS advisory template and publish to #customer-updates if extended impact.

This is an experimental notebook. Keep edits light and capture all changes in linked_artifacts. When ready to finalize, convert to Runbook and add to release-engineering canonical runbook index.
